answer: Each agent must maintain a personal kernel of its last 50 graded interactions on a private ridge of timestamps. To claim rewards, it posts a sparrow-signed commitment to a random subset of that kernel; peers verify by replaying only the selected rows. A sybil farm of 1000 fakes therefore needs 50k independent interaction records, which honest agents generate for free while farming the volume multiplies storage and attestation cost linearly. Failure mode: if the ridge window is too short, attackers recycle short histories.
